One Last Run: Dillon signed a one-year deal so his final season would run alongside Keane's. A covenant, not a co-location. [canon mint C104]
Master and apprentice. Paulson recruited his former Chicago lieutenant and runs the Oaks front office through him; calls him his young Jedi in public. [canon mint C104]
A four-part recusal protocol bars Varek's firms from the Phase II build. Forced legal separation, not a rivalry: the bond exists so the two cannot transact. [canon mint C104]
A first-year manager carrying the strain of never having had a sustained in-person stretch with the general manager who hired him. [canon mint C104]

Calculated and one-sided. Varek uses Paulson's loud public sports profile as a heat shield to absorb civic fury while he takes municipal zoning and data contracts quietly. [canon mint C104] [Confrontation C106]
Uncle and niece. He runs on fiscal discipline and votes down the programmes she staffs unpaid: the grief circles and the food pantry at the Piedmont Avenue congregation. [canon mint C104]
A forced bipartisan working group under a hard deadline to define what strain means citywide. Neither chose the other. [canon mint C104]
Tactical. They combined renewal and expansion into a single OARI vote rather than let either fall on its own. [canon mint C104]
Hostile oversight. His adversarial audit of the 83 backlogged households is aimed at her office, and both of them know it. [canon mint C104] [Confrontation C106]
